quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #22
										  					
  

60 Questions • Passing Score 50

questions.question: When parking your vehicle on a hill, what should you do?

options.text: One of your rear wheels should touch the curb.
Use your parking brake and leave the vehicle in park.
Your front wheels should be parallel to the road if there is no curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your parking brake and leave the vehicle in park.
questions.explanation: Always use your parking brake and put your vehicle in park when parked on a hill. If there is no curb, turn your front wheels away from the center of the road. This prevents the vehicle from rolling if the brakes fail.

questions.question: What should you do at a flashing red traffic light?

options.text: You are traveling in the wrong direction.
Treat it like a stop sign.
You cannot go until it turns green.

questions.correctAnswerText: Treat it like a stop sign.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means stop. Come to a complete stop at the stop line or before the crosswalk. Yield to all other traffic and pedestrians before going.

questions.question: If your tires lose contact with the road surface, what should you do?

options.text: Slow down by shifting into a lower gear.
Ease your foot off the gas pedal.
Slow down by pumping the brakes quickly and firmly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ease your foot off the gas pedal.
questions.explanation: Ease off the gas pedal and stay off the brakes. Do not try to stop or turn until your tires grip the road again.

questions.question: When driving past a car that just parked on the side of the road, you should:

options.text: Assume the driver will open the door as you pass.
Assume the driver will wait for you to pass before opening the door.

questions.correctAnswerText: Assume the driver will open the door as you pass.
questions.explanation: Assume the driver may open the door as you approach. Be very careful when driving near parked cars.

questions.question: Railroad crossings should always be considered:

options.text: Safe to cross because trains rarely come.
A place where you must stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Dangerous.
questions.explanation: Railroad crossings are always dangerous. Look and listen for trains from both directions. Follow all signs and signals. Only cross when you are sure it is safe.

questions.question: Regulatory signs are usually what color and must always be obeyed?
questions.correctAnswerText: White
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs are white with black markings. They control traffic movement and you must always obey them.

questions.question: A fire engine is following you on a two-lane street with no emergency lights on. What should you do?

options.text: Stop as quickly as you can.
Speed up to get out of the way.
Slow down, move to the right, and stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive normally.
questions.explanation: If an emergency vehicle is not using its siren or lights, you do not need to move. Just drive normally.

questions.question: When can you cross double solid yellow lines?
questions.correctAnswerText: To turn into a driveway.
questions.explanation: Double solid yellow lines mean no passing or lane changes. You can only cross them to turn left into or out of a driveway or to make a legal U-turn.

questions.question: What does this sign warn you about?

options.text: A series of curves is ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: A series of curves is ahead.
questions.explanation: This yellow and black warning sign alerts drivers to upcoming curves in the road.

questions.question: What must you do when a school bus is picking up or dropping off children?

options.text: Stop, no matter which direction you are traveling.
Stop only if you are going the same direction.
Slow down and be ready to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop, no matter which direction you are traveling.
questions.explanation: Always come to a complete stop before reaching a school bus when it is picking up or dropping off children, no matter which direction you are traveling.

questions.question: When you park uphill on a street with a curb, what should you do?

options.text: Keep the front wheel straight and set the parking brake.
Turn the front wheels away from the curb.
Turn the front wheels toward the curb.
Turn the back wheels into the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn the front wheels away from the curb.
questions.explanation: Turn your wheels away from the curb on an uphill street. If your brakes fail, your car will roll away from traffic, not into it.

questions.question: In bad weather, you should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Steer and brake smoothly.
questions.explanation: In bad weather, make smooth movements. Do not slam on the brakes or make sharp turns. These actions make it harder to control your car.

questions.question: What is a "No zone"?

options.text: The blind spot of a large vehicle
An area designated for motor vehicles

questions.correctAnswerText: The blind spot of a large vehicle
questions.explanation: "No zones" are the large blind spots around trucks and big vehicles. Avoid staying in these areas when driving smaller cars.

questions.question: What do pennant-shaped signs mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: No passing zones.
questions.explanation: Pennant-shaped signs show no passing zones. The sign will have text that says "No Passing" to confirm.

questions.question: If you have a sudden tire blowout, what should you do?
questions.correctAnswerText: Use the brakes lightly.
questions.explanation: If a tire goes flat, hold the steering wheel tight and keep the car straight. Slow down by lifting your foot off the gas and using light braking.

questions.question: When you see this sign, you:

options.text: Are approaching a railroad crossing and should prepare to stop.
Will always stop at the upcoming railroad crossing.
Should stop and wait for a signal before crossing the railroad tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Are approaching a railroad crossing and should prepare to stop.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a railroad crossing is coming. Look and listen for trains. Slow down and be ready to stop. Wait for any trains to pass before you go.

questions.question: When is the highway most slippery?

options.text: If it has been raining for several hours.
If it has just begun to rain.
If it has been raining for one to two hours.

questions.correctAnswerText: If it has just begun to rain.
questions.explanation: Roads are slipperiest when rain first starts. Dirt and oil on the road mix with water and create a greasy film.

questions.question: If your headlights fail, what should you try first?

options.text: Turn the headlight switch on and off.

questions.correctAnswerText: Try the dimmer switch.
questions.explanation: If your headlights fail, first try the dimmer switch. This often turns them back on.

questions.question: What does a single broken white line down the center of a two-lane road mean?

options.text: Lanes are moving in opposite directions and drivers are not permitted to pass.
Lanes are moving in opposite directions and drivers are permitted to pass when it is safe to do so.
Lanes are moving in the same direction and drivers are not permitted to pass.
Lanes are moving in the same direction and drivers are permitted to pass when it is safe to do so.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lanes are moving in the same direction and drivers are permitted to pass when it is safe to do so.
questions.explanation: White lines separate traffic moving the same way. A dashed white line means you can pass when it is safe.

questions.question: When you get in a car to drive, what should you adjust first?
questions.correctAnswerText: Your seat
questions.explanation: Adjust your seat first so you are comfortable and can see the road. Then adjust your mirrors and steering wheel based on your seat position.

questions.question: When changing lanes to the left, where should you glance to check your blind spot?
questions.correctAnswerText: Over your left shoulder.
questions.explanation: Look over your shoulder in the direction you want to move to check your blind spot.

questions.question: When can you legally turn left at a red traffic light after stopping?

options.text: You are traveling on a two-way street and turning onto a two-way street.
You are traveling on a one-way street and turning onto another one-way street.
You yield to all other traffic at the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: You are traveling on a one-way street and turning onto another one-way street.
questions.explanation: After a complete stop, you may turn left at a red light only if you are on a one-way street turning onto another one-way street. Make sure there are no signs prohibiting this turn.

questions.question: How far should a driver sit from the steering wheel?
questions.correctAnswerText: 12 to 15 inches
questions.explanation: If your vehicle has an airbag, sit at least 12 to 15 inches from the steering wheel. Do not move your seat so far forward that you cannot steer properly.

questions.question: What does a posted speed limit sign mean?

options.text: The exact speed at which you must travel to avoid a ticket.
The maximum safe driving speed under ideal road and weather conditions.
The maximum safe driving speed under all road conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: The maximum safe driving speed under ideal road and weather conditions.
questions.explanation: A speed limit sign shows the maximum legal speed for that road. You may need to drive slower than the limit if conditions are not ideal, such as rain or poor visibility.

questions.question: When turning left onto a one-way street, which lane should you turn into?

options.text: The lane closest to your previous lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The lane closest to your previous lane.
questions.explanation: Always turn into the lane closest to the lane you are leaving.

questions.question: What color are regulatory signs?
questions.correctAnswerText: White.
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs tell drivers about traffic laws they must follow. These signs are usually white rectangles with black, red, or green letters or symbols.

questions.question: What should you do at an intersection with a flashing red light?

options.text: Slow down and drive carefully through the intersection.
Turn either right or left, since the road is blocked ahead.
Stop at the intersection and wait for a flashing green light.
Stop at the intersection, then proceed as traffic allows.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop at the intersection, then proceed as traffic allows.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means you must come to a complete stop. Then you can proceed when it is safe.

questions.question: What are signs called that require drivers to follow a specific instruction?
questions.correctAnswerText: Regulatory signs.
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs tell drivers what they must do. Breaking this rule can result in a penalty.

questions.question: What lights should you use when driving in fog?

options.text: It makes no difference which lights you use.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your low beams.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights when driving in fog, rain, or snow.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Reserved parking for persons with disabilities.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not enter.
questions.explanation: This sign is posted where drivers are not allowed to enter. You may see it on one-way streets or if you try to enter an expressway ramp the wrong way.

questions.question: When changing lanes, how do you check your blind spots?

options.text: Use both inside and outside rearview mirrors.
Turn your head and look over your shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head and look over your shoulder.
questions.explanation: Turn your head to check your blind spots before every lane change.

questions.question: You are driving in the center lane of an expressway and cars keep passing you on both sides. What should you do?
questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the right lane.
questions.explanation: Stay in the right lane unless you are passing or turning left. Use the right lane if you are driving slower than the flow of traffic.

questions.question: When should you leave extra space in front of your vehicle when stopped?
questions.correctAnswerText: On an incline.
questions.explanation: Leave extra space in front of your vehicle when stopped on an uphill slope. This prevents a collision if the vehicle in front of you rolls backward.

questions.question: What do regulatory signs tell drivers?

options.text: They warn of dangers in every location where there is a hazard.
They show what you must or must not do.
They are diamond-shaped and yellow or green.
They warn you are approaching a school zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: They show what you must or must not do.
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs are usually rectangular with black markings on white. They tell drivers what they must or must not do, such as speed limits or turning rules.

questions.question: You park facing uphill where there is no curb. After setting the parking brake, what should you do with your wheels?

options.text: Turn them toward the edge of the road.
Turn them away from the edge of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn them toward the edge of the road.
questions.explanation: Turn your front wheels toward the right edge of the road. This helps the vehicle roll off the road if the brakes fail.

questions.question: What happens to your field of vision when you increase your speed?

options.text: It makes it easier to see cross traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: It decreases.
questions.explanation: As you drive faster, your field of vision becomes narrower. You must stay alert to hazards because you can see less.

questions.question: At intersections, crosswalks, and railroad crossings, what should you always do?

options.text: Stop, listen, and proceed with caution.
Look left and right to see what is coming.
Slowly pass vehicles that appear to be stopped without reason.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look left and right to see what is coming.
questions.explanation: Look to both sides of your vehicle before proceeding at intersections, crosswalks, and railroad crossings. Make sure no one is coming from either direction.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: U-turns are not allowed.
questions.explanation: A red circle with a red line through it means the action is prohibited. Do not make U-turns where this sign is posted.

questions.question: What does a flashing yellow X on a lane control signal mean?

options.text: The signal is about to change to a red X.
The signal is about to change to a green arrow.
You may only use this lane to turn left.
You may drive slowly in this lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may only use this lane to turn left.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow X means you can use that lane only to make a left turn. Lane control signals change throughout the day to manage traffic flow.

questions.question: What does a diamond-shaped sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Warning.
questions.explanation: Diamond-shaped signs warn drivers of hazards or special conditions ahead. They are usually yellow or orange.

questions.question: You can only get an Operating Under the Influence (OUI) conviction if you fail an alcohol test.
questions.correctAnswerText: False
questions.explanation: You can get an OUI conviction even if you refuse to take an alcohol test. A police officer can testify about how you were driving. This testimony alone can result in an OUI conviction.

questions.question: Your vehicle is blocking traffic after an accident. What should you do?

options.text: Move your vehicle off the road if possible.
Do not move your vehicle under any circumstances.
Wait for police to arrive before moving your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move your vehicle off the road if possible.
questions.explanation: After a minor accident, move your vehicle off the road if you can. Do not leave the scene without giving your information and helping if needed.

questions.question: An oncoming car is heading toward you in your lane. What should you do?

options.text: Honk your horn, turn right, and speed up.
Honk your horn, turn left, and brake.
Honk your horn, turn right, and brake.
Stay in your lane, honk your horn, and brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Honk your horn, turn right, and brake.
questions.explanation: Honk your horn to get the other driver's attention. If they do not move, steer right. Do not swerve left because the other driver might correct at the last second and you could still crash. Brake hard and steadily. Every mile per hour you slow down reduces the impact.

questions.question: A broken yellow centerline means:

options.text: You can pass on the right when the way ahead is clear.
You can pass on the left when the way ahead is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can pass on the left when the way ahead is clear.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow centerline means you can pass another vehicle on the left as long as there is no oncoming traffic. Never cross a solid yellow centerline to pass.

questions.question: You are exiting the interstate. When should you reduce your speed?

options.text: About halfway through the deceleration lane.
As you approach the deceleration lane.
Immediately upon entering the deceleration lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Immediately upon entering the deceleration lane.
questions.explanation: Keep your normal speed until you enter the deceleration lane. Then slow down to the posted speed for the exit ramp.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Low clearance.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the overpass ahead has low clearance. Do not drive through if your vehicle is taller than the height shown on the sign (in this case, 13 feet 6 inches).

questions.question: You see a yellow traffic light ahead and have not entered the intersection yet. What should you do?

options.text: Speed up to get through before the red light.
Slow down and carefully drive through.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a safe stop.
questions.explanation: When you see a yellow light, prepare to stop. If you are already in the intersection, drive through it quickly.

questions.question: You do not need to use your parking brake during an emergency roadside stop.
questions.correctAnswerText: False
questions.explanation: Always use your parking brake during an emergency roadside stop. Turn on your emergency flashers to warn other drivers.

questions.question: Road signs for public recreation areas are what color?
questions.correctAnswerText: Brown.
questions.explanation: Brown signs show cultural, historical, or recreation areas. They are helpful when traveling in unfamiliar places.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Steep downgrade.
questions.explanation: This yellow warning sign alerts drivers to a steep hill ahead. Adjust your speed to avoid brake damage or a crash.

questions.question: When you see a flashing yellow arrow at a traffic signal, what should you do?

options.text: Merge into the lane in the direction of the arrow.
You may turn left, but first yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
You have the right-of-way and oncoming traffic must stop for you.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may turn left, but first yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow arrow means you can turn left in that direction. However, oncoming traffic has a green light, so you must yield to them and to pedestrians.

questions.question: A fully loaded tractor-trailer going 55 mph can take up to ____ to stop completely.
questions.correctAnswerText: 400 feet
questions.explanation: Large trucks need much longer distances to stop than cars traveling at the same speed. A fully loaded tractor-trailer going 55 mph needs almost 400 feet to stop.

questions.question: Can you pass on a two-lane road when there is a single solid yellow line on your side of the center line?
questions.correctAnswerText: False
questions.explanation: You can only pass when the broken yellow line is on your side. A solid yellow line on your side means you cannot pass.

questions.question: When a green arrow changes to a solid green light, what can you do?

options.text: You may still turn, but you must yield to oncoming traffic.
You can no longer turn and must go straight.
You still have the right-of-way to turn.
You no longer need to turn in the direction the arrow showed.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may still turn, but you must yield to oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: When a green arrow becomes a solid green light, you may still turn in that direction. However, you must first yield to pedestrians and oncoming traffic.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: One-way traffic.
questions.explanation: This sign tells drivers the direction they must drive on a one-way street.

questions.question: What does a red flashing traffic light mean?

options.text: The same as a solid red light.
The same as a stop sign.
The same as a yield sign.
The same as a caution sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: The same as a stop sign.
questions.explanation: A red flashing traffic light means stop. Come to a complete stop and proceed when it is safe.

questions.question: You are crossing an intersection when you see an emergency vehicle with its siren and flashing lights coming. What should you do?

options.text: Stop immediately in the intersection until it passes.
Pull to the right of the intersection and stop.
Continue through the intersection, then pull to the right and stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Continue through the intersection, then pull to the right and stop.
questions.explanation: If you are in an intersection when an emergency vehicle approaches with flashing lights and/or siren, finish crossing. Then drive to the right and stop. Always yield to emergency vehicles.

questions.question: You want to enter the freeway but you don't see a gap in traffic. What should you do?

options.text: Keep your speed and force other drivers to make a gap.
Slow down on the ramp to wait for a gap.
Stop at the end of the ramp to wait for a gap.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down on the ramp to wait for a gap.
questions.explanation: Slow down on the ramp to wait for a gap. Do not stop at the end of the ramp or you won't have enough room to speed up before entering traffic.

questions.question: If your vehicle starts to skid, what should you do?

options.text: Turn your steering wheel into traffic.
Turn your steering wheel in the direction of the skid.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your steering wheel in the direction of the skid.
questions.explanation: Stay calm and steer in the direction of the skid to regain control.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Keep driving at your current speed.
There is a traffic signal ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is a traffic signal ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a traffic signal is coming up ahead.
